en: Son of a Brahmin
The most promising young man in the city; his father is a priest.
zh: 全城最被看好的年轻人，他的父亲是祭司。

en: No one knows his family name, yet everyone calls him “the Brahmin's son”—the name in the lexicon that most resembles the hero.
zh: 他姓什么没人知道，但人人都叫他「婆罗门之子」——词条库里最像主角的那个名字。

en: The Vessel Unfilled
He is the most learned in this house, and the least content.
zh: 他是这个家里最博学、也最不满足的人。

en: The pride of every Brahmin in the city—the son who left home to seek the way.
zh: 全城婆罗门的骄傲——那个离家求道的儿子。

en: I Will Follow You
One announced that he would go; one followed, his face pale.
zh: 一个是宣布要走的人，一个是脸色苍白跟上来的人。

en: The companion who always lagged a step behind, following him as one follows a god.
zh: 那个总落后一步、把他当神明一样跟从的伙伴。

en: Standing Until Dawn
One old, one young, facing each other through a little window until dawn.
zh: 一老一少，隔着一扇小窗对峙到天亮。

en: The one who, at the last, laid his hand on his son's shoulder.
zh: 最后把手放上儿子肩膀的人。

en: I Will Not Tire
The one standing in that little window.
The Brahmin's son.
Eagle and Jackal
The young man who practised most harshly and learned the fastest.
zh: 修得最狠、学得最快的那个年轻人。

en: The elder's proudest disciple—yet in his heart he is already doubting it all.
zh: 长老最得意的弟子——可他心里正在怀疑这一切。

en: Anesthetic
The one who has begun to find asceticism a “conjurer's trick.”
zh: 开始觉得苦修是「鬼把戏」的人。

en: The Samana who made a parable of rice wine.
zh: 那个拿米酒打比方的沙门。

en: The Rising Spiral
One still believes in this path; one no longer does.
zh: 一个还信这条路，一个已经不信了。

en: The doubter is always the one walking half a step ahead.
zh: 质疑者总是那个走在前面半步的人。

en: Rumour and Hypnosis
Of the four “people,” one is not there at all; he lives only in rumour.
zh: 四个「人」里有一个根本不在场，他只活在传闻里。

en: The old man who bowed and blessed once his eyes were held, and the disciple who held them.
zh: 被盯住眼睛就鞠躬祝福的老人，和盯人的那个弟子。

en: The Teaching at Jetavana
He speaks not a word; merely walking, he makes himself known.
zh: 他不讲一句话，光走路就让人认出来。

en: People call him “the Blessed One.”
The Night of Taking Refuge
This is the first time in his life he has not followed his friend.
zh: 这是他人生第一次没有跟着朋友走。

en: From now on he belongs to the Buddha's order.
zh: 从此他属于佛陀的僧团。

en: The Crack in the Teaching
The one who dared say to his face that “the teaching lacks a corner,” and the one of whom it was said.
zh: 敢于当面指出「教义缺了一角」的人，和被指出的人。

en: The parting gift of words was about “excessive cleverness.”
zh: 临别赠言是关于「过分的聪明」。

en: Awakening
The one who decided “no longer to flee himself.”
zh: 决定「不再逃避自己」的人。

en: The hero of this story.
The I in Rumour
This man with the alms bowl—the children of the city can call his name.
zh: 托钵的这个人，城里的孩子都叫得出他的名字。

en: What he speaks of, again and again, is suffering, and the path that extinguishes it; these years, young men from every place have set out because of him.
zh: 他一遍遍讲的是苦，以及熄灭苦的那条路；这些年来，各地的年轻人都为他上路。

en: Lay Out One More Robe
The clearing is packed with people, yet he first concerns himself with two hungry guests from the woods.
zh: 空地上坐满了人，他却先关心两个饿着肚子的林中来客。

en: One word from him—“follow us”—and that very night someone took off worldly clothes and put on the yellow robe.
zh: 他一句「跟从我们」，当晚就有人脱下俗衣、披上黄衣。

en: The Missing Corner
Someone said to his face that his teaching lacked a corner; he did not refute it.
zh: 有人当面说他的教义缺了一角，他没有反驳。

en: After sitting a night under the tree, he spent the rest of his life speaking of the same path.
zh: 他在树下坐了一夜之后，用余生讲同一条路。

en: The Ferryman and the River
The seeker who has just left the Buddha and taken the road alone, penniless.
zh: 刚离开佛陀、独自上路的求道者，身无分文。

en: The ferryman said he would come back one day to repay him—remember this river.
zh: 船夫说，他日后还会回来报答——记住这条河。

en: The Lady in the Palanquin
One in the palanquin, one outside it.
zh: 一个在轿子里，一个在轿子外。

en: The mistress of this garden; her red lips like a fresh fig.
zh: 这座园子的女主人，红唇像新鲜的无花果。

en: A Poem for a Kiss
One named a price, one bargained—his counter-offer was three arts and a poem.
zh: 一个开价，一个还价——他还的价是三种本事和一首诗。

en: The one whose red lips are like a fresh fig.
zh: 红唇如新鲜无花果的人。

en: The Merchant's Interview
One examines, one answers—the one answering called fasting the wisest thing.
zh: 一个考校，一个应答——应答者把斋戒说成最聪明的事。

en: The richest man in the city, and the one most given to worry.
zh: 全城最有钱、也最爱发愁的人。

en: Love and Commerce
Three people: the one who teaches “the art of love,” the one anxious over losses, and the one anxious over neither.
zh: 三个人：教“爱的艺术”的、为亏本着急的、一个都不着急的。

en: The anxious one is the master; the unanxious one was once a Samana.
zh: 着急的那个是东家，不着急的那个曾是个沙门。

en: Death of the Songbird
The one who dreamed the caged bird had died.
The owner of the golden cage.
Om at the Riverbank
He meant to destroy himself; one word saved him.
zh: 他想毁掉自己，一个字救了他。

en: That syllable Brahmin children learn to say from the first.
zh: 那个音节，婆罗门的孩子从小就会念。

en: How Beautiful the World Is
The one who has just begun to see the world with “another pair of eyes.”
zh: 刚刚“换一种眼睛”看世界的人。

en: Still the same hero.
I Am No Longer a Beggar
The one just made new at the river, changing his own skin.
zh: 刚在河边焕然一新的那个人，正在给自己换新皮。

en: The hero of the story, still without a coin to his name.
zh: 故事的主角，这时还一文不名。

en: The Courtesan's Introduction
She pushed open door after door for him.
zh: 她替他推开一扇又一扇门。

en: Red lips, gold bracelets, a fan of feathers.
Writing, Though Fair
The one who has just passed a strange interview.
zh: 刚通过一场奇怪的面试的人。

en: The one who takes “fasting” as his capital.
You Do Not Know True Love
She said the words “you do not know true love.”
zh: 她说出了“你不懂得真爱”。

en: The bird she keeps lives in a golden cage.
The Potter's Wheel
The one who has caught “the rich man's disease.”
He was once a Samana.
Unrecognised
The old monk who watched over the sleeper, and the seeker who does not look like a seeker.
zh: 守护酣睡者的老僧，和不像求道者的求道者。

en: When young, the old monk had a friend he honoured most.
zh: 老僧年轻时有个最敬爱的朋友。

en: One Third
A master who has made his lodger's “not caring” a sickness of the heart, and the lodger who will not take it to heart no matter what.
zh: 一个把门客的「不在乎」当成心病的东家，和那个怎么也不肯上心的门客。

en: The one who worries is the grey-haired man who takes business as his life; the one spoken of came from the woods, and can think, wait, and fast.
zh: 发愁的是斑白头发、把生意当性命的那位；被议论的那个从林子里来，会思想、会等待、会斋戒。

en: At Last He Has Learned to Worry
He had waited so long for that man to fret over money—and now that it had come, he could not be glad.
zh: 他终于等到那个人肯为钱着急，反倒高兴不起来。

en: Hair gone grey, shrewd and full of care; the counting-house lamp often burned past midnight.
zh: 斑白头发，精明多虑，账房的灯常常亮到半夜。

en: He Left No Word
A man left without a word, and not a coin was touched—those left behind were more frightened than if the money had been lost.
zh: 一个人不告而别，钱一文没动——留下的人比丢了钱还慌。

en: The frightened one was the master who turned the ledger three times; the one who left never came back to this city.
zh: 慌的是那位把账翻了三遍的东家；走掉的那个，从此再没回过这座城。

en: My Name Is Vasudeva
That old promise—'You will come back and repay me'—was fulfilled today.
zh: 多年前那句「你会回来报答我」，今天应验了。

en: The man who knew best how to listen—he spent his whole life rowing this river.
zh: 最会倾听的人——他一辈子都在这条河边摇船。

en: The Ferryman's Apprentice
The new apprentice later asked the question about 'time'.
zh: 新上手的那个徒弟，后来问出了「时间」的问题。

en: He had once been a rich man in the great city.
The Snakebite
Of the four, two were old men, and one was a child.
zh: 四个人里，有两个是老人、一个是孩子。

en: The mother had been the most beautiful in the city; the old man at the fire was an old acquaintance of hers.
zh: 母亲曾是全城最美的人；生火的老人与她是旧相识。

en: old
Death at the Ferry
She had meant to see the Buddha a last time, and met her old lover first.
zh: 她本想去看佛陀最后一眼，却先见到了旧情人。

en: Her lips had once been like a fresh fig.
zh: 她的嘴唇曾像新鲜的无花果。

en: old
old
Broken Bowls
An eight-year-old spoiled by his mother.
zh: 被母亲惯坏的八岁孩子。

en: The child's father, when young, had once kept his own father sleepless a whole night.
zh: 孩子的父亲，年轻时也曾让他的父亲一夜难眠。

en: old
Broken Oars
Who stole the fares and broke the oars?
zh: 谁偷走了船费、折断了船桨？

en: The man who told the father to let go had no children of his own.
zh: 劝父亲放手的那个人，自己无儿无女。

en: old
Ten Thousand Sounds Become Om
The one word into which ten thousand river-sounds flowed.
zh: 万千河声汇成的一个字。

en: The word a Brahmin's child could chant from childhood.
zh: 婆罗门的孩子从小会念的那个字。

en: old
The Last Bow
Only the third time did he truly 'see' his friend.
zh: 他第三次才真正「看见」自己的朋友。

en: That smile he had seen on only one other face.
zh: 那个微笑，他只在一个人脸上见过。

en: old
old
Newborn Infant
The man who had just died once by the river and come back to life.
zh: 刚在河边死过一回又活过来的人。

en: The one this story is about.
Year upon Year
He no longer speaks doctrine aloud, yet the ledger in his heart still runs, year after year.
zh: 他嘴上不再讲道理，心里那本账还一年一年记着。

en: That white-haired apprentice by the river never went home again after he left.
zh: 河边那个白发的学徒，离家之后再没有回去过。

en: He Has Her Eyes
The man who has just learned he has a son.
zh: 刚知道自己有个儿子的人。

en: The child's father.
old
A Night Listening to the River
The man who sat outside the hut all night.
zh: 在草舍外坐了一整夜的人。

en: He has just seen the child's mother away.
old
The Listener
The man who teaches 'listening' seldom speaks much himself.
zh: 教「倾听」的人，自己从不多话。

en: The ferryman.
Before the Garden Gate
The man who stopped at the gate of his old lover's garden.
zh: 在旧情人的园子门口停下脚步的人。

en: The one he pursued was his son.
old
Send Him Back to the City
The one who urged him to 'send him back to the city'.
The childless old man saw more clearly than the father.
zh: 无儿无女的老人，看得比父亲更清。

en: old
Farewell, River
The man who left the ferry to his apprentice.
The ferryman.
old
Seeking and Finding
The man who sought all his life, and the man who had long since 'found'.
zh: 追寻了一生的人，和早已「寻见」的人。

en: The old monk in all his life took refuge with only one teacher.
zh: 老僧这一生只皈依过一位导师。

en: old
old
The Seventeenth Boat on the Mound
He sat on the mound counting the boats that passed, and would not eat a mouthful.
zh: 他坐在土丘上数河里过去的船，一口饭也不肯吃。

en: Eight years old, his mother just dead at the ferry; he will not acknowledge the white-haired man.
zh: 八岁，母亲刚死在渡口，他不肯认那个白头发的人。

en: The River Would Not Carry Him
One wanted to buy a passage home with other people's money; the other said it was the river's money.
zh: 一个想用别人的钱买一趟回城的船，一个说那是河的钱。

en: The small one is eight; the old one has poled all his life, and never loses his temper.
zh: 小的那个八岁；老的那个撑了一辈子船，从不生气。

en: The Thing Thrown into the Water
He counted the coppers, crossed the river, and before he left broke one thing on the boat and threw it in.
zh: 他数着铜板过了河，走之前把船上的一样东西折断扔了。

en: He wanted to force that father who never lost his temper to lose it once.
zh: 他想逼那个从不发火的父亲发一次火。
